chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Abi al-Mughirah, from al-Sakuni, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: On the Day of Judgment, a caller will cry out, 'Where are the oppressors and their helpers? And those who brought their ink, who tied their bags, or who held the pen for them? Gather them along with them.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the specific helpers of oppressors on the Day of Judgment according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal* highlights the concept of *sharikah* (partnership) in oppression, extending liability beyond the ruler to the administrative class. It specifically identifies scribes and record-keepers who prepared ink, tied bags, or held pens as co-participants, illustrating how bureaucratic facilitation constitutes a share in the injustice. This underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the accountability of those who enable tyranny through their professional services.
